title: Consciousness as Field Resonance: From Ego-Filtered Ontology to Differentiation-Dominant Dynamics
description: Proposes a field-based ontology of consciousness in which awareness corresponds to a differentiation-dominant resonance regime constrained by regional feedback. Re-analyzing propofol EEG (Chennu et al. 2016), the study finds spectral differentiation (Omega) tracks conscious state with a double dissociation, while global causal integration (kappa) is weak and a pre-registered multiplicative model C = Omega × kappa is falsified. An exploratory parietal product shows a strong effect, and a negative Omega–kappa correlation supports a balance (trade-off) constraint.

Omega_spectral_differentiation.description: Spectral differentiation (spectral entropy) indexing internal structured complexity.

kappa_causal_integration.description: Causal integration measured via transfer entropy (regional or global).

product_measure_C.description: Pre-registered multiplicative model of consciousness (F1) — falsified in this analysis.

balance_constraint.description: Balance (trade-off) between differentiation and integration in conscious regimes.

key_results.main_finding: Omega strongly tracks conscious state with a double dissociation; global kappa is weak, and the pre-registered product C = Omega × kappa is falsified; exploratory parietal product is strong and the Omega–kappa correlation is negative.

sealed_predictions.statement: In independent, dose-matched propofol datasets with responsive vs drowsy subgroups, Omega (full band) will exhibit a double dissociation (responsive increases; drowsy decreases) with a large between-group effect (Cohen's d ≳ 1.0).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Failure to observe opposite-signed Omega changes across matched responsive vs drowsy groups in at least two preregistered replications.

sealed_predictions.statement: Across moderate sedation at matched doses, corr(Omega, kappa) will be negative (trade-off) at the group level.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Consistently positive corr(Omega, kappa) (> +0.2) in two or more independent, preregistered datasets.

sealed_predictions.statement: A parietal/posterior regional product C(parietal) = Omega × kappa will outperform Omega alone in classifying conscious state (Cohen's d > 1.5) in a preregistered replication.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: C(parietal) failing to exceed Omega’s effect size (by ≥ 0.3 d units) in a preregistered, independently collected dataset.

sealed_predictions.statement: Removing delta (using 4–40 Hz) will reduce Omega’s effect size relative to full-band Omega in sedation paradigms.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Equal or larger effect sizes for Omega(4–40 Hz) compared to full-band Omega in two or more independent sedation datasets.

kill_criteria: KC1: In at least two preregistered, independent datasets spanning anesthesia or comparable perturbations, global or regional integration metrics (e.g., transfer entropy, Granger, phi-like measures) consistently outperform Omega in predicting conscious state (each with Cohen's d ≥ 0.8) while Omega shows weak effects (|d| ≤ 0.2), and corr(Omega, kappa) is positive (> +0.2), contradicting the differentiation-dominant, balance-regime claim.

KC2: The dose-matched double dissociation for Omega fails to replicate twice (no opposite-signed changes between responsive and drowsy groups; or both groups change in the same direction), undermining the claim that consciousness, not drug level, determines Omega’s direction.

KC3: A preregistered replication of the exploratory regional effect shows that C(parietal) does not exceed Omega (difference in d < 0.3) and/or reverses direction in two independent datasets, undermining the regional-feedback constraint.

KC4: Closed-loop or stimulation interventions that selectively increase kappa (integration) without increasing Omega lead to reliable increases in conscious report or behavioral responsiveness, overturning the differentiation-dominant priority.

KC5: Across diverse states (wake, NREM/REM sleep, anesthesia, psychedelics), pooled analyses demonstrate a robust positive relationship between Omega and kappa (meta-analytic r ≥ +0.2 with p < 0.01), contradicting the balance (trade-off) constraint central to the model.
abstract: The ontology of consciousness remains constrained by a hidden assumption: that awareness is a local property generated inside isolated systems. This paper argues that consciousness is best understood as a resonant regime within a universal dynamical field, where systems differ by their capacity to form differentiated, self-referential dynamical structures. Empirical analysis of EEG under propofol sedation shows spectral differentiation (Omega) tracks conscious state with a double dissociation. A pre-registered multiplicative model is falsified (F1). A differentiation-dominant, regionally constrained resonance model is supported.
empirical_pillars: Pillar 1: Differentiation is primary (Omega d=1.50, double dissociation)
Pillar 2: Global integration not detected; regional integration candidate (kappa d=0.42, Parietal C d=2.10)
Pillar 3: Balance, not maximisation (negative Omega-kappa correlation r=-0.27)

revised_model.falsified: Consciousness = Omega x kappa (both maximised globally)
revised_model.supported: Consciousness = differentiation-dominant resonance regime, constrained by sufficient regional feedback, in a balance regime

testable_predictions.test: kappa vs hit-rate; linear wins = fails

conclusion: Consciousness is best described as a high-differentiation resonance regime within a universal dynamical field, stabilised by regional feedback rather than global integration. The ego is not the origin of awareness but a structured expression within this regime. Consciousness is becoming a physics problem, not a metaphysical one.
